llm.summary: The skill is a clearly disclosed TikTok business-account automation guide with significant but purpose-aligned browser and OS-input access.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a logged-in TikTok browser profile, CDP access, clipboard use, screenshots, cron operation, and macOS Accessibility input control; this is powerful but disclosed and directly tied to the UI-only automation purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single markdown skill with no executable scripts; it requires user-provided tools and configuration rather than installing hidden code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are unusually explicit about scope: reply-only workflows, phase gates, quotas, human handoff on platform controls, honest bot disclosure, and no attempts to bypass captchas or rate limits.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists local operational logs under a workspace memory directory and optionally sends recaps to a webhook only if configured; retention and data minimization are described, though account handles and lead usernames may be recorded locally or in opted-in alerts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capability matches the stated purpose: scheduled inbound TikTok DM and comment replies for an owned business account, with explicit limits, qualification checks, stop conditions, and no outbound prospecting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving an automation terminal control over a logged-in TikTok browser and macOS Accessibility input. Use a dedicated low-privilege session, keep the alert webhook unset unless operators need it, review local logs for retained usernames, and pause the skill whenever TikTok shows a challenge, block, or account-risk warning.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector:clean] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues; artifact review found the sensitive browser, OS-input, cron, and local-log behavior disclosed and purpose-aligned.
[VirusTotal:clean] expected: VirusTotal telemetry showed no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this supports but does not determine the benign verdict.
